A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DERD-Net and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix A report original DERD-Net experiments on MVSEC and DSEC, including depth-estimation results, reflection tests, patch-size sensitivity and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds depth estimation using estimated camera poses, a reprojection experiment and downstream camera-tracking results in Section 4.6 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The Sub-DSI processing, 3D convolution, GRU, dense outputs, MAE loss and two-model ensemble remain unchanged. V2 clarifies ray origins and normalized-depth rescaling. The reprojection loop is introduced as an evaluation protocol rather than a revision to the proposed depth estimator.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates depth estimation on MVSEC indoor_flying 1–3 and DSEC Zurich_City_04_a. V2 adds offline camera tracking across Zurich_City_04_a–f, including five previously unused sequences, and depth-estimation scenarios with noisy poses from odometry systems.

E2.justification: SGM and GTS are added to the DSEC comparison in v2 Tables 3 and 15; v1 Tables 4 and 12 omit them, although both already participate in MVSEC comparisons. The existing deep-stereo comparator set is retained. ESVO2 supplies poses for robustness experiments rather than a separately scored competing depth method.

E3.justification: V2 introduces protocols using ES-PTAM/ESVO2 poses, offline depth-to-tracking-to-DSI reprojection, and camera tracking against maps constructed using ground-truth poses. Tracking adds ATE and ARE RMSE evaluation. The original benchmark splits, training epochs, filters and depth metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and Appendix A.3 add substantial tests of sensitivity to estimated poses and feedback from DERD-Net's own depth errors. Appendix A.1 adds computational-cost analysis to the patch-size study. The reflection, patch-size and per-sequence no-ensemble analyses already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed values, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both describe the same two independently initialized ensemble models and cross-validation arrangements. V2's percentage changes and tracking RMSE values are performance summaries, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Tables 5 and 8–10 report pose-noise, reprojection and tracking outcomes, including 17.07 cm tracking ATE RMSE on zc04a. Existing DERD-Net benchmark scores remain unchanged. DSEC ESVO changes from 3.88 m MAE and 3.40 million points to 3.93 m and 9.40 million points; the PDFs do not explain this replacement. DSEC SGM/GTS scores and an averaged no-ensemble row are also added.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–3 for Sub-DSI normalization, convolution outputs and GRU representations are retained. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs. The added depth-rescaling explanation is an implementation clarification.

C1.justification: The abstract's central method, accuracy, completeness and efficiency claims are unchanged. The introduction and conclusion add explicit claims of robustness to imperfect camera poses and demonstrated downstream applicability, extending the earlier general claim of suitability for SLAM.

C2.justification: V2 adds an accuracy-versus-computation rationale for the chosen patch size, explains excluded MVSEC sequences, and interprets pose-noise results with attention to changing point coverage. Appendix A.4 explicitly limits tracking results to offline maps built using ground-truth poses, without accumulated drift or direct comparability to online SLAM. These substantive qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies moving-camera ray casting, output-depth rescaling and layer resizing in the existing patch-size experiment. Section 4.7 documents preprocessing workload, CPU hardware and approximately 45/26/0.2 ms for DSI creation, fusion and pixel selection. V2 also explicitly states that code, trained models and videos are provided, while retaining the existing project link and training hyperparameters.

R1.justification: V2 adds references concerning event-based SLAM, ESVO2, deep visual odometry and simulation-to-real transfer, and strengthens discussion of practical pose sources. Its central positioning as learning depth from geometrically constructed DSIs remains unchanged. Publication updates and duplicate-reference cleanup do not represent new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the top-level narrative are retained, with selective explanatory rewrites. The deep-stereo comparison moves from Section 4.8 to 4.5; detailed patch-size and reflection discussions move into Appendix A.1–A.2; detailed benchmark tables form Appendix B.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column NeurIPS layout. V1 Tables 3–4 merge into v2 Table 3, existing sensitivity displays are consolidated and relocated, and new pose/tracking Tables 5 and 8–10 are introduced. The three figures retain their substantive content but are resized and relabeled.

improvement.justification: V1's SLAM-suitability claim lacked estimated-pose and tracking tests. V2 substantially strengthens practical validation through estimated-pose experiments on both benchmarks, reprojection testing and offline tracking on six DSEC sequences. It also discloses preprocessing costs and the offline-map limitation. Changing point coverage limits direct robustness comparisons, and Tables 8–9 apparently mislabel centimetre-scale errors as metres, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and transparency.
